data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's separating property conflates two structurally distinct rules under 'additive number-conservation', but the mechanism it gives for Rule 184 — particle count conservation forcing cyclic-shift dynamics and bounding cycle length to W — is mechanically false for Rule 184 on a ring. Rule 184 is the traffic rule; 110->10 (particle moves right), 101->110 (annihilation), 011->110, etc. The number of 1s is NOT conserved: pattern 110 evolves to 100, destroying a particle. Thus the claimed invariant slice C(W,k) and cyclic-shift equivalence are false, and the property misclassifies Rule 184 by attributing a conservation law it does not have. SRC_001 made a different (also dubious) decomposition claim, so this is target-specific.
